newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Facts and figures on Indonesian elections.
newsitem.headline: Facts and figures on Indonesian elections.

text.p: Following are facts and figures on the Indonesian national and local elections:
- Voting Thursday, May 29, after five-day cooling-off period following April 27-May 23 campaign.

- Three political parties legally permitted to take part: ruling Golkar party, which won 68 percent in last elections in 1992, Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) which won 17 percent, and Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) which won 15 percent.
- Polls open from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0100 GMT-0700 GMT).
- Electoral Commission says results from the archipelagic nation of over 17,500 islands will be known with a week; major trends should be known within 24 hours.
- Electorate: 124.7 million of population of 200 million.
- Minimum voting age 17, younger if married.
- Seats in House of Representatives: 500, of which 425 elected and 75 alloted to the military which does not vote.
- Members elected by proportional representation by party lists in multi-member constituencies. Number of members varies.
